title: The field as an object: sharp field states, reduced descriptions, conventions

key_results.statement: For a sharp and stationary field state, $C(\Psi\otimes\varphi)=((C_{\rm red}+e_f)\Psi)\otimes\varphi$ with the reduced contract $C_{\rm red}=C_{br}+\sum_j n_j B_j\otimes\mathbb 1_r$; exact, linear independence not used.
Exact evolution for a sharp and stationary field: $\Psi(\lambda)=e^{-ie_f\lambda}\,(e^{-iC_{\rm red}\lambda}\Psi_{br})\otimes\varphi$ for every $\Psi_{br}$ and every $\lambda$.

Both views are pure, $V=\lvert\Psi_{\rm red}\rangle\langle\Psi_{\rm red}\rvert$ and $V_f=\lvert\varphi\rangle\langle\varphi\rvert$ constant: the field does not become entangled with the body or the other objects.
Every schedule of readings on $b$ and $r$ has exactly the statistics of the reduced description with contract $C_{\rm red}$ and start $\Psi_{br}$.

A contract $C'$ on $\mathcal H_{br}$ reproduces all schedule statistics for every start iff $C'=C_{\rm red}+\Delta$ with $\Delta$ real, diagonal in the joint places and $[\Delta,C_{\rm red}]=0$; a real constant always qualifies.

Order estimate for $\lambda\to0$: $1-\operatorname{Tr}V^2=\frac{2\lambda^{2k_0+2}}{((k_0+1)!)^2}\lVert\sum_j(B_j-\langle B_j\rangle)\Psi_{br}\otimes\omega_j^{(k_0)}\rVert^2+O(\lambda^{2k_0+3})$, where $k_0$ is the smallest $k$ with some $\omega_j^{(k)}=(\Phi_j-n_j)C_f^k\varphi\neq0$.

For sharp $\varphi$ and linearly independent $\mathbb 1_b$, $B_j$: the view of $\{b\}\cup r$ is pure for every $\Psi_{br}$ and every $\lambda\ge0$ iff $\Phi_jC_f^k\varphi=n_jC_f^k\varphi$ for all $j$ and all $k\ge0$; without linear independence the condition is sufficient but not necessary.

Under (2.11), exactly $\Psi(\lambda)=(e^{-iC_{\rm red}\lambda}\Psi_{br})\otimes e^{-iC_f\lambda}\varphi$: the reduced description with the same $C_{\rm red}$ exists, the view of the field is pure and moves.

Two-place field with $\Phi_1=\lvert1\rangle\langle1\rvert$, $C_f=\gamma(\lvert0\rangle\langle1\rvert+\lvert1\rangle\langle0\rvert)$, $\varphi=\lvert0\rangle$: sharp with $n_1=0$, and (2.11) fails at $k=1$.

For a sharp $\varphi$ violating (2.11) the lowest power is $\lambda^4$: $1-\operatorname{Tr}V^2=\frac{\lambda^4}{2}\sum_{j,j'}\Gamma_{jj'}\langle C_f\varphi\vert(\Phi_j-n_j)(\Phi_{j'}-n_{j'})\vert C_f\varphi\rangle+O(\lambda^5)$ with $\Gamma_{jj'}$ the covariance of $B_j$, $B_{j'}$ in $\Psi_{br}$ (order estimate).

Under linear independence the replacements at fixed $B_j$ that leave $C$ unchanged are exactly $\Phi_j\to\Phi_j+a_j\mathbb 1_f$, $C_f\to C_f+c\,\mathbb 1_f$, $C_{br}\to C_{br}-\sum_ja_jB_j-c\,\mathbb 1_{br}$ with real $a_j$, $c$.
Under (2.20), $n_j\to n_j+a_j$, $e_f\to e_f+c$, $C_{\rm red}\to C_{\rm red}-c\,\mathbb 1_{br}$: neither the numbers $n_j$ nor their differences $n_j-n_{j'}$ are well defined.

$\hat C=C_{\rm red}+e_f\mathbb 1_{br}=(\mathbb 1_{br}\otimes\langle\varphi\rvert)C(\mathbb 1_{br}\otimes\lvert\varphi\rangle)$ depends only on $C$ and $\varphi$; $C_{\rm red}$ is well defined up to a real multiple of the identity.

The on-site block $\Omega_x=(C_{\rm red})_{xx}=\hat C_{xx}-e_f$ is well defined up to a constant common to all positions and $\Omega_x-\Omega_{x'}$ exactly; its split into body, medium and field parts is not well defined.
A medium that is also the field is sharp for $\Phi_x=\mathbb 1_c+gxY$ and gives $d_0>0$ iff $Y\chi=y\chi$ and $\sigma_X>0$; such $\chi$ exist iff $X$ is not a function of $Y$.

Under (2.25) the factor $\Phi_x$ amounts exactly to the number $n_x=1+g\,y\,x$: the body has the own term $C_b+\sum_xn_x\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert\otimes G$ and is recorded through $K_x=\kappa xX$ alone.

If the medium is not sharp, $V_b=\sum_{y,\xi}w_{y\xi}\lvert\phi^{(y,\xi)}\rangle\langle\phi^{(y,\xi)}\rvert$ with body contracts $C_b+\sum_x\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert\otimes((1+gyx)G+\kappa\xi x)$: profile slope $gy$ and record gradient $\kappa\xi$ occur with the joint distribution of $Y$ and $X$ in $\chi$.

open_issues: The expansions (2.10) and (2.14) hold for λ → 0; no bound on the remainder and no range of λ on which the leading term dominates is derived.
A field whose operators Φ_j do not commute with its own term C_f is treated only through the criterion (2.11) and the expansion (2.10); its view at finite λ is left to a later package.
Starts in which the field is entangled with the body or the other objects, and readings on the field, are outside the question; in Step 8 readings on the medium are not treated.

Which operator G the field multiplies, and what the well-defined differences of on-site blocks (2.23) mean for a clock and for motion, belong to 03-clock-and-fall; a package that uses a profile n_x must fix the listing or work with (2.22) and (2.23).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: under λ → λ/s and C → sC all formulas are homogeneous, and the coefficient of (2.10) scales as s^(2k_0+2), compensating λ^(2k_0+2).
Φ_j equal to the identity for all j (includes a field with one place): every field state is sharp with n_j = 1, (2.11) holds, the field decouples and C_red = C_br + Σ_j B_j.

Two-place field with one index and a two-place body: direct computation gives 1 − Tr V² = β²γ²λ⁴/2 for the example (2.13), equal to (2.14); in the static case (2.18) gives sin²(βλ)/2, whose leading term equals (2.10) with k_0 = 0.
